To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
M1 RNA has at least two centers for binding of Mg2+, one of which is involved in catalysis and the other of which is important for substrate recognition.
the metal ion cofactors of M1 RNA are located at two different centers in the catalytic subunits of RNase P.

the catalytic activity and the metal ion-induced cleavages of M1 RNA can be modulated by the addition of various metal ions and that the sites of cleavage of the RNA can be used to identify the centers for binding of the metal ions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the sites of cleavage in the catalytic RNA of RNase P and the identification of the centers for binding of the metal ion cofactor and inhibitors of the enzyme.
the identification of the centers for binding of cofactor ions in M1 and P RNA, and the role of these centers in the catalytic activity.
the identification of the centers for the binding of Mg2+ in the catalytic RNA of RNase P, M1 RNA, and the substrate, precursor tRNA(Tyr), and with their role in the processing reaction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
metal ion binding to RNA, as well as to other ligands, is a very important and general feature in biological systems.
the cleavage of the substrate by metal ions is a process that involves the participation of the substrate, M1 RNA, and the cofactor, metal ions, in a concerted manner.
the RNA subunit, M1 RNA, of RNase P is a metalloenzyme, which is cleaved at several specific sites by the metal ions that are essential for its catalytic activity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the metal ion cofactors, as well as the metal ion inhibitors, of M1 RNA cleavage are located at the sites of cleavage and at the sites of binding of the substrate and cofactor.
metal ions are required for the cleavage of M. RNA and that the metal ions are bound in specific centers in M1 RNA and in the substrate.

the metal ion-induced cleavages of M1 RNA are a useful probe of the location of phosphate residues that are involved in the binding of metal ion cofactors in M1 RNA and that the cleavage sites are located in centers for the binding of Mg2+ and Mn2+, and in a center for the substrate binding.
The main takeaway from our work is that
M1 RNA, P RNA, and other ribozymes are subject to cleavage at specific sites by metal ions, and that these sites can be exploited to identify the locations of metal ion binding centers in RNA.
the RNA subunit M1 RNA of the ribonuclease P from E. coli has two different centers for the binding of Mg2+ that are involved in its catalysis of cleavage of precursor to tRNA.
metal ion cofactors, inhibitors, and substrates can be used to identify sites on RNA for binding of metal ion cofactors that are important for catalysis.
